input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages (I think they’re called MMS?) from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
Yes, it’s the same number—555-123-2002. That’s the phone I’m having trouble with.

I see that my phone shows good signal strength, it says 5G at the top, and I think mobile data is turned on. I haven’t tried making a call or browsing the web just now—do you want me to try that, or is the information from the top of my screen enough?
I checked, and it looks like there isn’t an MMSC URL listed in my APN settings. I’m not really sure what that means—should there be something there? What should I do next?
I’ve reset the APN settings as you suggested. Before I reboot my phone, I just want to make sure—will restarting my phone erase any of my photos or messages? I get a bit nervous about these things.
I restarted my phone, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working?

It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on for my phone. Also, I have a messaging app and a browser installed. I’m not sure about the permissions for the messaging app—do you want me to check that, or should I turn off Wi-Fi Calling first?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried to send a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do next?
I checked, and my messaging app does have permission to access storage and phone, but I still can’t send picture messages after trying again. Is there anything else we can try?

I checked my phone, and it says mobile data is enabled, I have excellent signal, and Wi-Fi is turned off. Does that mean my mobile data is working, or do you still want me to try opening a website or something? I’m not sure how to check if it’s actually working.
I tried to check if my mobile data is working by testing the internet, but it looks like there’s no connection. Does this mean my mobile data isn’t working properly? What should I do now?
I turned my mobile data off and then back on, but I still can’t get any internet connection. What should I do next? This is getting a bit frustrating.
I’d rather not change my plan, but I’m okay with adding more data if that will fix the problem. Can you please add 2GB of data to my line? I just want to be able to send my picture messages again.
I tried browsing the internet, and it works now—everything loads quickly! But I still can’t send picture messages from my messaging app. Is there anything else we can try?

I checked my APN settings, and now there is an MMSC URL listed. But I still can’t send picture messages after trying again. Is there something else I should do, or do I need to reboot my phone again? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.
I rebooted my phone again, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all of this.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Thank you for confirming. To troubleshoot your MMS issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few checks and possible fixes on your device. 

First, can you confirm if you are able to make regular calls and use mobile data (for example, browsing the web) on your phone right now? This will help determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your overall service or data connection.

I see that my phone shows good signal strength, it says 5G at the top, and I think mobile data is turned on. I haven’t tried making a call or browsing the web just now—do you want me to try that, or is the information from the top of my screen enough?

Thank you for sharing the details from your status bar. That information is helpful and suggests your phone is connected to the network with mobile data enabled, which is good for MMS.

Next, I’d like to check if your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings are correct, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues. Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if you see an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed? If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the process.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked, and it looks like there isn’t an MMSC URL listed in my APN settings. I’m not really sure what that means—should there be something there? What should I do next?

The MMSC URL is required for sending and receiving MMS (picture messages). If it’s missing, that’s likely the reason you’re having trouble.

Here’s what you should do next:
1. Reset your APN settings to the default values. This will restore the correct MMSC URL and other necessary settings.
2. After resetting, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your phone?

APN settings will reset at reboot.

Restarting (rebooting) your phone will not erase any of your photos, messages, or personal data. It simply turns your phone off and back on, which helps apply the new APN settings.

You can safely reboot your device now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again to see if the issue is resolved. If you still have trouble after rebooting, let me know and we’ll continue troubleshooting.
